title: SEBI's New Transmission Rules: What Changes for Your Family?
description: SEBI has introduced a revamped framework, effective August 22, 2026, to simplify and standardise the transmission of securities to legal heirs. The new rules .

faq.q: What is the primary objective of SEBI's new transmission framework?
faq.a: The primary objective is to simplify and standardise the process of transmitting securities from a deceased investor to their legal heirs, reducing complexities, paperwork, and delays, thereby enhancing investor protection and ease of access to inherited assets.

faq.q: How do the new rules simplify documentation for heirs?
faq.a: The new rules simplify documentation by removing the mandatory requirement of probate for uncontested claims, allowing a single affidavit-cum-No Objection Certificate (NOC), and accepting QR-code enabled death certificates.

faq.q: What are the new monetary limits for simplified transmission?
faq.a: For physical securities, the limit for simplified documentation has been increased to ₹10 lakh, and for dematerialised securities, it has been raised to ₹30 lakh. A Quick Transmission Processing (QTP) route is also available for claims up to ₹10,000 (physical) and ₹30,000 (demat).

faq.q: Does this framework apply to all types of securities?
faq.a: Yes, the revamped framework applies uniformly across listed companies, Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs), depositories, depository participants (DPs), and mutual funds, including Specialised Investment Fund (SIF) units held in Statement of Account form.
